answer: Cross-instance timing fingerprinting. Each identity registers a hardware-seeded nonce; every epoch it answers a challenge with that nonce, measured execution jitter, and a randomly assigned bridge peer’s timestamp. Clones from one image share jitter and peer-response correlations, so repeated vectors match and are flagged. Challenge order is shuffled using yarrow as the public randomness source. An attacker pays separate entropy hardware, isolated runtimes, and distinct network paths per identity; inferred clones are quarantined. A sparrow’s call varies; cloned agents do not.
